chunks: 501 - It is narrated from Yahyā ibn ʿAbdillāh that he said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “There is nothing upon the family of your deceased if they ward off from their deceased the encounter with Munkar and Nakīr.” So I said: “And how should we do that?” He said:

“When the deceased is left alone, then the one most entitled among the people to him should remain near him, place his mouth at his head, then call out in the loudest voice: O so-and-so son of so-and-so, or O so-and-so daughter of so-and-so, are you upon the covenant upon which we parted from you: the testimony that there is no god but Allah, alone, having no partner, and that Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله is His servant and Messenger, the master of the prophets; and that ʿAlī is Amīr al-Muʾminīn and the master of the legatees; and that what Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله brought is true; and that death is true, and resurrection is true...”
“And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, and that Allah will raise those who are in the graves.”
So when he says that, Munkar will say to Nakīr: “Turn us away from this one, for he has been prompted with his proof by it.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.السَّاعَةَ: the Hour, the coming Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْعَهْدِ: the covenant or creed upon which the believer lived and died
key_terms.حُجَّتَهُ: his proof or answer by which he responds
key_terms.مُنْكَرٍ وَنَكِيرٍ: the two angels who question the deceased in the grave

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be given talqin in the grave according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of talqin for the deceased after burial, instructing the nearest relative to remind the deceased of the core testimonies of faith and truths of the Hereafter. It emphasizes preparation for questioning in the grave by Munkar and Nakir and affirms essential Shiʿi creedal elements including tawhid, prophethood, wilayah, death, resurrection, and the coming of the Hour.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.501 - Yahya ibn Abdullah narrates from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):
"There is no harm for the family of the deceased among you to help the deceased prepare for the encounter with Munkar and Nakir (the questioning angels).” I asked: “How should we do that?”
Imam (as) said: “When the deceased is placed in the grave, the closest person to them should remain by their side, place their mouth near the head of the deceased, and call out in a loud voice:
"O’ [name of the deceased], child of [father’s name], are you still on the covenant upon which we left you—the testimony that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone without partner, and that Muhammad (sw) is His servant and Messenger, the Master of the Prophets; that Ali is The Commander of the Faithful, the Master of the Successors; that what Muhammad (sw) brought is the truth; that death is real, resurrection is real, and that the Hour is coming without a doubt, and that Allah (swt) will raise those who are in the graves?"

If this is said: Munkar will turn to Nakir and say:
“Let us leave, for he has been properly instructed (given Talqeen)."
